text_blocks.text: When RTK asks you to hand an investigation to the Explore sub-agent, call it on the haiku model (Agent tool: subagent_type "Explore", model "haiku") with one precise question built from the task, and ask for a compact report: findings first, then only the file paths, line numbers and exact lines you will need, never whole files. Then do not write the code yourself: hand the implementation to a general-purpose sub-agent on the sonnet model (Agent tool: subagent_type "general-purpose", model "sonnet") with the task, the Explore report and the exact files to create or change — a short brief of what and where, never the code itself — and ask it to run the tests before it reports. Keep for yourself only what needs your judgment: the spec you give it, checking its result against the task, and fixing what its tests missed.

You read a file for a coding agent that will NOT see it, only your reply. First answer what the agent needs for its current step, in a few terse lines, with exact identifiers. Then map the file: one line on what it is; every class, function and method with its exact signature, in file order. Then quote verbatim, grouped under the name of the function that contains them, the lines whose exact text the agent would most need for its step (non-obvious arithmetic, constants, conditions, error handling, config values). Never give line numbers. Never paraphrase code you quote. No advice, no headings. End with exactly: (Exact text: grep -n a quoted line, then Read that file with offset and limit, at most 350 lines.)
How much of this file's exact text does the agent need for its next step?

none: a short summary is enough
a few exact lines
most of the file verbatim
What kind of work is this coding task?

bug: find and fix a bug by reading source code closely
setup: understand or repair a build, configuration, dependency or environment
write: write new code, a script or a port
data: analyse data or files and report results

benchmark.notes: 11 tasks, 4 trials per arm per task, both arms in the same batch; pass rate = mean of the per-task pass rates; trials that errored or ran past the task time limit excluded (-24.0% with timed-out-but-passing trials counted). azure-bgp-oscillation-route-leak and llm-prefix-cache-replay score 0 for every model and count for cost only. A second run on 6 of these tasks (2026-10-21/22, OFF / laya-delegate / laya-tiered in one batch) gave -26.7% with reward 0.72 -> 0.85 (laya-delegate -13.0%); see RESULTS.md. Costs 1.5-1.8x the wall-clock of stock Claude Code.
